title: Senior's toolkit: Windows
summary: The Windows-only commands a Windows admin types every week, with the switches that matter. All of them need Windows (most need an elevated session to change anything).

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: Windows
steps.body: **Windows only.** These run in PowerShell 7 and Windows PowerShell 5.1 on Windows. Reading is usually allowed for any user; changing services, the HKLM registry, tasks and the Security log needs an elevated (Run as administrator) session.

steps.prompt: `Get-ScheduledTaskInfo` shows `LastTaskResult : 2147942402` for a task that runs `pwsh.exe -File C:\Ops\Nightly.ps1`. What does it mean?
options: 0x80070002: the system cannot find the file (pwsh.exe or the script path is wrong)
steps.explain: Convert it: `'{0:X}' -f 2147942402` is `80070002`, the Win32 error 2, *file not found*. Check that `pwsh.exe` is on the PATH of the account the task runs as (or give its full path) and that the script exists.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: Use CIM, not WMI; filter events with `-FilterHashtable`; write registry values with the type the reader expects; register tasks from code with `pwsh.exe -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File "..."` and a time limit. And test Windows functions with mocks, so they run in CI before they run on a server.
